results.title: 7 Best Rill Alternatives in 2026 for BI-as-Code and…
results.content:
The 7 best Rill alternatives in 2026 are:

1. Luzmo: best overall for native customer-facing analytics and product-team ownership
2. Lightdash: best for dbt-first analytics-as-code teams
3. Cube: best for a headless semantic layer serving many applications
4. Metabase: best for approachable open-source BI
5. GoodData: best for governed enterprise and multi-tenant analytics
6. Preset: best for managed Apache Superset
7. Grafana: best for operational and observability dashboards

## Rill alternatives at a glance [...] One category note that saves real money: if your dashboards are fundamentally about infrastructure health, latency and alerting rather than business questions, you're shopping in the wrong aisle. The Grafana alternatives for monitoring-heavy teams address that need directly, and no BI tool will match them on it.

## Best alternatives to Rill

### 1. Luzmo: best overall Rill alternative for customer-facing analytics

Rill begins with analytics engineering.

Luzmo begins with the product user.

That distinction matters when the main job is shipping analytics inside a SaaS application rather than building a version-controlled BI stack.

#### Visual ownership for product teams

Luzmo Studio gives product managers and analysts a visual drag-and-drop builder. [...] ## Why look for a Rill alternative?

Rill is a modern platform with a clear point of view.

It gives developers and analytics engineers a version-controlled way to manage the analytics stack, while AI agents can read and modify the same code-defined assets.

The reasons to compare alternatives come from that same design.

### The code-first model may not match the people who own customer analytics

Rill defines sources, metrics and dashboards in SQL and YAML.

It now includes visual editing, but the platform still positions code, Git and the terminal as central to the workflow.

That works well when analytics engineers own the product.

A SaaS team may want product managers, analysts or customer-facing teams to create and update dashboards without managing a code repository.

Hi Product Hunt, I'm William! I made Rill because I want to always stay in the flow.

As an ADHD, I never liked code-switching. My best ideas for work come when I'm supposedly not working at all: watching something for fun, reading things and following a rabbit hole, looking at how someone else solved a problem. Then when an idea hit me, I'd have to stop, switch to coding agents, find the project and explain it all, and most of the time I just didn't. [...] Subscribe

AI Workflow Automation

Rill is an AI-native browser built around the Claude Code and Codex you already use. Browse normally, then press ⌘E on any page to turn what you're looking at into a task for your agent. Rill finds the right project, passes along the context, and the agent works while you keep browsing. It also sorts your tabs into themes, turns your history into days you can search, and brings every project your agents are working on into one place. Free, on the plan you already have. [...] Rill is my way of removing that code-switching. It's a browser with your Claude Code or Codex working alongside you. When something on a page gives you an idea, you say so right there, and an agent starts on it in the right project. You don't have to spend time looking for the right folder, rephrasing everything you just saw on the web, and you don't switch in and out of work mode. The work goes on with you in the flow.

This matters now more than ever. Agents have shortened the distance between ideas to output near zero. So the bottleneck is capturing the idea at the moment you have it. That moment is nearly always while you're taking something in, and that is what a browser is for.
